files.content:
# Gamestage UI sounds

The default sound for every `sfx` cue in `packages/tokens/tokens.json`, one
MP3 per cue name, mono, 64 kbps, about 150 KB for the whole set. Five cues
come in three takes: `correct`, `countdown`, `rankUp`, `reward` and `xp`.
GSUI-38.

A game opts in with `npx gamestage-ui add sounds`, which copies these files to
`public/gamestage/sfx/`, then passes a file adapter to the provider:

```tsx
import { GameFeelProvider } from './components/gamestage/cues'
import { createDefaultSoundAdapter } from './components/gamestage/sound-set'

const sound = createDefaultSoundAdapter()

<GameFeelProvider sound={sound} muted={soundOff}>
  <Game />
</GameFeelProvider>
```

## Choose a take

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `pick` | `{ [cue]: number }` | take 1 | Plays that take for that cue: `{ rankUp: 2, reward: 3 }`. A take that does not exist plays take 1 |
| `vary` | `true` or a list of cue names | off | Rotates a cue through its takes, never the same one twice in a row, for a cue a fan hears many times a round. A rotated cue ignores `pick` |
| `volume` | 0 to 1 | 0.6 | How loud every cue plays |

| Cue | Take 1 | Take 2 | Take 3 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `rankUp` | rising two-note chime | three quick marimba notes | synth blip stepping up |
| `reward` | warm bell with a sparkle | glassy ding, rising tail | short harp flourish |
| `countdown` | soft wooden tick | one marimba note | warm, low digital beep |
| `xp` | soft rising sparkle with reverb, 0.9 s | another take | another take |
| `correct` | bright two-note chime | another take | another take |

Take 1 is `<cue>.mp3` and take n is `<cue>-<n>.mp3`. Replace any file with your
own of the same name to change one sound, or use `createFileSoundAdapter` with
your own `base` to replace them all.

## Where they came from

Generated with ElevenLabs' sound generation on 17 October 2026 by
`scripts/generate-cue-sounds.mjs`, on a paid ElevenLabs plan (Creator), whose
terms give the subscriber the commercial rights to what it generates. They
ship under this repository's MIT licence. The prompt for each cue is in that
script, and it is the only design input: to change a sound, change its prompt
and run the script for that cue.

Each file is cleaned the same way so the set sounds like one set: leading
silence removed, cut to the cue's length (400 ms or less; `xp` 0.9 s with a
soft reverb tail, `win` and `celebrate` 1.5 s), and brought to one mean
loudness. Generation is not repeatable, so these files are the ones that were
listened to and approved; regenerate a cue only to replace it.
